winterStorage.note: LL-33 experimental game balance. Feed: about 9.5 lb/cu ft for small square hay bales (~50 lb in 5.25 cu ft) and 40 lb/cu ft for bagged poultry feed; 10 cu ft of household bins without a shed. Above-ground tanks freeze after their freezing degree-days (°F below 32, accumulated; thaw days melt) — bigger tanks hold out longer; the pond and Earthship cisterns are treated as frost-protected. Insulation multiplies the tolerance by 4; a thermostatic heater draws kWh per gallon per freezing degree-day.

toolRules.note: LL-34 experimental balance from the catalog row: 150 lb of wood per 2.2 h is about 68 lb/h, 1.7× the 40 lb/h of hand-gathered deadfall; 0.2 gal gasoline per 2.2 h is 0.091 gal per working hour.
LL-34 experimental balance from the catalog row: 30 lb of green biomass per 2.1 h is about 14 lb/h, 2.4× the 6 lb/h of hand-cut wild greens. Applies to green biomass only, not foraged food.
LL-34 experimental balance. The catalog row (20 lb per 0.5 h) would imply 13× a 3 lb/h clay bank, but a broadfork loosens beds rather than digging clay, so the boost is capped at 2×.

soilFertility.note: LL-35 experimental game balance. Fertility 1 is the catalog's full yield; yield = 30% + 70% × fertility, capped at 110%. A full year of cropping draws 0.35 (annual beds) or 0.15 (perennials), scaled by realized yield; the catalog's own compost rate replaces exactly that draw. Bought-soil beds start at 1, dug-in plots at 0.7, perennial plantings at 0.8. A pound of manure counts as half a pound of compost. A clover cover crop adds 0.2 a year to gardens within 100 ft, shared by their area. LL-44: cover crop seeding sows 200 sq ft of gardens within 30 ft and adds up to 0.15 a year while the beds rest (outside the growing season), shared by garden area and scaled by the share of its seed sown in the late-summer window and by its upkeep met.

householdRoles.note: LL-36 experimental game balance. A school-age child needs about 70% of an adult's food, water and supplies and does a quarter of an adult's work; an elder needs 90% and works half. Skills rise with each person's share of the hours practiced: building up to 50% faster DIY, growing up to 25% more harvest, gathering up to 30% more per hour, each half-learned after 150, 100 and 100 hours. Below 40 wellbeing a person may fall ill (up to 2% a day at 0), losing a week of work; building and chainsaw work carry a small chance of injury per hour (two weeks at 30% work).

finance.note: LL-37 experimental game balance, not market quotes: tax on parcel acres at a fixed assessed value; insurance covers newly failed LL-28 equipment only, not routine maintenance, livestock or buildings removed by the player.

riskEvents.note: LL-38 experimental game balance, not hazard predictions. Each eligible risk draws every 28 days from a separate saved stream, then warns before starting. Predators retain the LL-31 stream and guardian/housing protection. Operational mitigation is measured on the previous day: nearby birds, bat habitat or hedgerow soften pests; compost piles soften disease; enclosed shelter reduces smoke exposure. Batteries/generators, stored food/water/fuel and rain collection bridge supply interruptions.

transportAccess.note: LL-39 experimental game balance. Market orders, physical supply deliveries and sale collection share one 10-mile trip or $25 delivery per day. Commuting miles follow the job catalog transport-to-work-hours ratio at hours actually allocated; paid travel is $0.50/mile. Remote work needs no commute. Town journeys use 10 person-miles per traveler or one $25 household ride; emergency fares can remain explicitly payable so zero-cash residents are not stranded. Operating vehicles provide only the previous measured day's mileage, with no multi-day bank.

waterInfrastructure.note: LL-40/41 experimental balance. Spring flow capped at site yield per hour (one hour-equivalent/day), shared across all boxes. First flush trades 5% rain capture for 25% lower filter labor after measured operation. Test kit issues precautionary warnings, not simulated lab results.

fodder.note: LL-42 experimental dryland balance. At 15 annual inches the 0.1-acre meadow yields about 200 lb/year; drier sites reduce yield linearly. Real-year drought scales that yield with a 20% floor. LL-34 scythe multiplier reduces cutting labor only; nominal hay yield never increases. Cutting reserves tool time before gathering, up to the existing 8 h/tool/day.

livestockInfrastructure.note: LL-43 experimental balance, not husbandry guidance. Eggs are set from stock and hatch after 21 counted days; an incubator day counts only with its 0.5 kWh and 80% upkeep met, a broody day only while her flock is active. More than two missed days loses the batch. A brooding hen stops laying. A staffed run protects up to 12 nearby birds from predator losses. A moved paddock kit raises its pasture's hay and greens up to 15%.

incomeTrade.note: LL-46 experimental balance. A CSA week short of produce or packing refunds the missing share and pays half of it again as a make-good. Ruth takes spare household labor in barter at $12/hour of goods value (70% trade terms already included), after the tutorial.
